children: Toro plans to spin off its liquefied petroleum gas carrier business.
The energy transportation company said Wednesday that its subsidiary AI Okto would become an independent company traded on Nasdaq.
AI Okto's initial assets include two LPG carriers and $45 million in cash, contributed by Toro. The company would be a pure-play LPG firm focused on establishing an AI-enabled operating model.

Toro shareholders won't receive fractional AI Okto stock. Instead, the distribution agent will aggregate and sell fractional AI Okto shares on the open market and distribute the cash proceeds to each holder on a pro rata basis.
Toro Chair and Chief Executive Officer Petros Panagiotidis would be appointed as AI Okta's CEO.
